_comment: The header row of every PacketPulse results CSV - the download beside a ticket (GET /diagnostic/{id}/report.csv), the Results API pull (GET /result/export.csv) and the scheduled push to an organisation's own server. An IT system's importer is written against this list, so columns are only ever ADDED, at the end - with one recorded exception, in 'retired': resolved_ip was taken out on 28 October 2026 at the customer's request (it read as the reflector's IP, not the user's; the user's addresses are user_ip and user_ipv6). A retired column never comes back under its old name. The Go writer's test asserts it writes exactly these; the integration suite asserts the server sends exactly these. checked_on is written in the organisation's own time zone with its offset (2026-10-21T11:30:00+05:30 in Mumbai); it was checked_on_utc until 22 October 2026, when the customer asked for IST. user_ip, added 26 October 2026, is the public IP a device test was filed from, as the server saw the caller; it is empty for a server sweep. user_ipv6, added the same day, is the device's public IPv6 as its own lookup found it (PacketPulse is reached over IPv4 and never sees it); empty when the device had no IPv6.

retired.why: customer request: remove the Resolved IP column from reports; the user's addresses are user_ip and user_ipv6
